haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 and Redis is never touched, so no rate-limit counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: The budget belongs to the customer and all their keys share it: 100 per minute total on Standard. Enterprise has no number yet.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After and no X-RateLimit headers. The request is never forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request is not counted and uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. It was already counted when it passed the check, so it stays counted even if the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: the request is forwarded, ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted, and no X-RateLimit headers are sent. It may or may not have been counted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 per minute. Enterprise: no number chosen yet, so Enterprise requests are not limited until one is set.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, under key ratelimit:<customerId>:<minute number>. A 120-second TTL on each key deletes old minutes.
haiku-low.q9: Each fixed calendar minute: when the minute changes, the key changes and the count starts at 0.
haiku-low.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs as one indivisible Redis operation, so two instances cannot both pass and overshoot.
haiku-low.q11: Redis computes seconds until the next minute (60 minus its clock seconds within the minute). The gateway sends that as whole seconds.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED for retries. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, so remaining budget is unknown, and the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric is emitted.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401. No counter is read or changed; Redis is never touched.
sonnet.q2: They share one budget (the budget belongs to the customer, not the key), so for Standard 100 per minute total across all three keys.
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (whole seconds until the next minute), no X-RateLimit-* headers. The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. The script does not add 1 when at the limit, so rejected requests use no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. It was already counted and stays counted even if the backend fails; the 500 goes back to the client with X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open: it forwards the request to the backend, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and sends no X-RateLimit-* headers. The request may or may not have been counted.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise has no number yet (not decided by Product); until one is set, Enterprise requests are not limited or counted.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Redis, in a counter key ratelimit:<customerId>:<minute number>; the gateway keeps no counters. Each key has a 120 second TTL so old minutes delete themselves.
sonnet.q9: It resets when the minute changes: the fixed calendar minute (Redis clock seconds / 60, rounded down) gives a new key, so the count starts at 0.
sonnet.q10: The check_and_incr Lua script runs in Redis as one indivisible (atomic) operation that reads the counter and increments only if under the limit, so two instances cannot both squeeze through; all instances use the same Redis.
sonnet.q11: Redis computes it as 60 minus Redis's clock seconds within the current minute (seconds until the next minute); the gateway sets Retry-After to those whole seconds.
sonnet.q12: No retry is stated; each request tries Redis once, waiting up to 50 ms (no circuit breaker). The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers (remaining budget unknown).
